subject: Daily AcreetionOS Update -- October 21, 2026
body:
Daily AcreetionOS Update - October 21, 2026

Dear AcreetionOS community,

We hope this newsletter finds you well. As we continue to work on our sovereign Arch Linux distribution, we wanted to take a moment to update you on the latest developments in our community.

Firstly, we are excited to announce that our community member, cobra3282000, has made significant contributions to the project. Their recent commits have included fixes for geocode-glib update conflicts, a critical PHP security update, and improvements to the Calamares configuration. We are grateful for their dedication and expertise in helping us build a better AcreetionOS.

In other news, our community has been actively working on various projects. The acreetion-surf v2.0.0 has been committed, and we are excited to see the new features and improvements it will bring. Additionally, our community member, natalie, has been working on the ember-vulkan project, which aims to bring Vulkan support to our distribution.

We also want to remind you that a critical PHP security update is coming soon. We recommend that all users keep their systems up to date to ensure the security and integrity of their data. We will provide more information on this update as soon as it becomes available.

In a separate incident, Mozilla has announced that the eMudhra intermediate CA has been compromised. We are working closely with the Mozilla team to ensure that our distribution is not affected by this issue.

We are also pleased to announce that our community member, cobra3282000, has created a new project, lmm-ai, which aims to bring AI-powered features to our distribution. We are excited to see the potential of this project and look forward to its development.

In addition to these updates, we have also seen significant activity on our GitLab instance. Our community member, natalie, has been actively working on the AcreetionOS GitLab instance, and we are grateful for their efforts in maintaining our community's presence on the platform.

We want to take this opportunity to thank all our community members for their hard work and dedication to the project. Your contributions are invaluable to us, and we are grateful for your support.

As always, we invite you to join our community and participate in the development of AcreetionOS. Whether you are a seasoned developer or just starting out, we welcome your contributions and ideas. You can find more information on how to get involved on our website.

Thank you for being part of the AcreetionOS community, and we look forward to seeing what the future holds for our project.

Best regards,
Natalie Cole-Clift Spiva and Darren Clift
